title: Tiangong space station
summary: China's permanently crewed orbital laboratory, now open to international payloads.
bodyHtml:
What This Is

Tiangong was assembled in orbit in 2022 and has hosted continuous crews since, with a three-module configuration and a planned expansion. It carries experiments in life science, materials and fluid physics, and China has invited foreign astronauts and payloads. For countries excluded from the International Space Station, it is the available alternative.

Status

Attribute Value
Development stage Early commercial
Estimated window 2022–2035
Confidence label Confirmed
Evidence Editorial synthesis of company, agency and press reporting
Compiled 18 November 2026

Related records

  • China's 15th Five-Year Plan

Investment Exposure

The station's value is diplomatic and scientific rather than commercial, but it anchors a supply chain of launchers and payload integrators.

What Would Change The View

  • Expansion module launch schedule.
  • Foreign payload and astronaut participation.
  • Commercial cargo providers.

Record Notes

Editorial brief, not an imported source note. Named milestones are drawn from company, agency and press reporting; forward dates are announced targets, not verified outcomes. No figure here is an audited statistic.
